reviewMethod: Read the Library of Juggling explanations and siteswaps
Inspect sampled frames from the public animated diagrams
Check event semantics, ballistic flight, held ownership, spatial constraints and actual bundled VRM cycle
Inspect selected front and diagonal browser poses
notClaimed: Continuous comparison against live human performance
Full mesh and clothing collision validation
Completion of every named Box or synchronous pattern

patterns.name: Bizarre Box
checked: Same hand catches its own 2T under the other forearm
Other empty hand passes underneath the self toss
Following 2 holds and carries the same ball before 2x
Two vertical columns; alternate sides over six sets

patterns.name: Karas' Box
patterns.notationRelation: Same repeating six-set sequence with a different starting set
checked: Replace Bizarre held return with another self toss
Two self tosses per hand in opposite directions
Underarm release and catch; opposite empty hand passes below the self toss
Six sets restore the movement and ball identities

patterns.name: Broken Box
checked: Both vertical columns stay on the performer right side
Opposite hand catches the outer column under the other forearm
Mirror moves both columns to the left

patterns.name: Swap Box
checked: Both simultaneous short transfers pass below the airborne 6
Four sets repeat the motion; twelve sets restore ball identities

patterns.name: Burst Box
checked: Alternate Broken Box on each side using a normal Box transfer
All 4 and 4x flights remain vertical
The hand returns to its own side after the underarm throw and receives the horizontal pass
Six sets restore movement and ball identities

patterns.name: Penman's Box
checked: Hold the 2 throughout the flourish
Carry the held ball above the descending inner column and outside the rising outer column before releasing the 2x
Throw the outer vertical 4x under the other forearm
Four sets restore movement and ball identities
Check forearm relation at the exact release event and preserve it during elbow refinement

patterns.name: Underarm Box
checked: Keep every 4 and 4x vertical; alternate sides over four sets
Release the outer 4x below the opposite forearm, then uncross to catch the horizontal pass
No vertical underarm catch; distinguish from Burst and Threaded Box

patterns.name: Gilligan's Box
checked: All high throws move from the inside to the outside of the throwing side
Catch each 4x with the opposite hand under the forearm
Keep that ball held through the 2 and carry it back to its own side before the next throw
Six sets restore movement and ball identities

patterns.name: Four Ball Box
checked: Pass twice in the same direction before changing sides
Throw the 6 from inside to outside with room for two airborne balls on one side
Four sets repeat the movement; eight sets restore the same ball identities

patterns.name: Four Ball Stacked Box
checked: Stack 8 and 4 on the same vertical line
High and low flights reach their peaks simultaneously
Four sets restore movement and ball identities

patterns.name: Synchronous Pistons
checked: Four distinct vertical lines; two synchronous pairs alternate across the width
Both hands move sideways together between the two pair positions
Spatial movement and ball identities repeat after two sets

patterns.name: Wimpy
checked: Both hands throw simultaneously to the opposite hand
Separate the crossing balls vertically in one frontal plane
Movement repeats every set; ball identities repeat after four sets

patterns.name: Reverse Synchronous Fountain
checked: The two hands throw at the same time, from outside toward the centre
Each ball is caught by its throwing hand; the source diagram shows two mirrored inward arcs
Movement repeats after one set and ball identities after two sets

patterns.name: Levels
checked: Four sets repeat the movement and ball identities
Outer columns stay vertical and are caught at zero vertical velocity
A top-to-middle slam is followed by a gravity-driven middle-to-low transfer
The low central 4x is claw-caught by the other hand
The central flight plane is about ten centimetres forward to separate it from the short passes
patterns.timingInterpretation: Follows the written apex-catch instruction. The animated diagram shows an outer catch below the ballistic peak, so exact timing equivalence with that diagram is not claimed.

patterns.name: Columns
checked: Throw the two outer balls together, then the central ball with one hand
The hand marked 0 remains empty, rather than holding a fourth ball
Every ball stays on its own vertical lane throughout flight and holding
Mirror changes the hand controlling the central ball
patterns.timingScope: Checks vertical lanes, paired throw order and hand ownership against the public animated diagram; exact human-performance timing is not claimed.

patterns.name: Four Ball Columns
checked: Both inner balls are thrown together, followed by both outer balls
Every ball stays on its own vertical lane throughout flight and holding
Two sets restore both movement and ball identities
Distinct from the alternating left-inner/right-outer pairing of Synchronous Pistons
patterns.timingScope: Checks vertical lanes, paired throw order and hand ownership against the public animated diagram; exact human-performance timing is not claimed.

patterns.name: HF / Crosses*
patterns.notationEvidence: Inferred from sampled video frames, not an author-provided notation.
checked: High ball released below the opposite forearm and caught by the opposite hand on its own side
Other ball remains held through the upper crossing and return toward its own side
White ball changes throwing hand; the model repeats the movement in two sets and each ball identity in six
Airborne high throws remain vertical, with no short 2x transfer added
Both underarm releases and the complete cycle pass the bundled VRM checks in both mirrors
limits: No exact frame-by-frame reconstruction of performance timing or depth

patterns.name: HF / Under-Arm-Box*
patterns.notationEvidence: The source table provides (4,2x)*. Sampled performance frames support underarm self throws and a high short transfer.
checked: Self 4 released below the opposite forearm on the opposite side of the body
The same throwing hand catches its 4 inward on its own side; no underarm catch relation is added
One ball remains the 2x transfer, while two separate balls remain the self 4s
The preceding 4 and the current 2x arrive at the same time
Full ball and bundled VRM cycles pass in both mirrors; movement and ball identities repeat after two sets
limits: Exact performance timing, depth and elbow angles are not reconstructed

connection.method: Separate the 4 flight plane, then move halfway toward the underarm endpoints before entering the unchanged target; reverse those steps to return.

patterns.name: HF / Reverse-Under-Arm-Box*
patterns.notationEvidence: The source table provides (4,2x)*. Sampled video frames support self 4s caught under the opposite arm and rising 2x transfers.
checked: Self 4 released inward on the throwing hand own side and caught by that hand on the opposite side of the body
Underarm relation applies to the 4 catch, not its release
Short 2x rises from a low release to the high hand; its catch coincides with the preceding opposite self-4 catch
One ball remains the 2x transfer and two separate balls remain self 4s
Movement and ball identities repeat after two sets; complete bundled VRM cycle passes in both mirrors
limits: Exact performance timing, depth and elbow angles are not reconstructed
Hand orientation follows ball velocity; exact source finger poses are not reconstructed

connection.method: Keep both original two-set sections. Add a two-set bridge on each side which separates the high and short flight planes before the underarm catch placement changes.

otherRemainingReferences: HF source variations and matrix combinations, plus additional synchronous patterns, retain their individual unverified status in sync-catalog.json.
eventConstraintMethod: Explicit per-hand underarm releases and catches are inserted at their exact phases into the arm cycle. Planning and smoothing preserve horizontal footprint and vertical gap; interpolation is checked again at those events.

sourceCorrections.reason: The primary page describes asynchronous multiplex throws. Do not count it as an implemented synchronous pattern.
